methods.titleHtml: Identify a minimal polynomial or prove integrality
methods.bodyHtml:
Recognise. Identify minpolyα,Q\mipy_{\alpha,\Q}minpolyα,Q​, prove α\alphaα is integral, or compute its trace and norm.

Write first. Find a polynomial f∈Q[x]f\in\Q\sbra{x}f∈Q[x] with f(α)=0f\bra\alpha=0f(α)=0 and declare the base field.

Solution route.

(i) If only integrality is required, clear the problem by finding any monic f∈Z[x]f\in\Z\sbra{x}f∈Z[x] with f(α)=0f\bra\alpha=0f(α)=0.

(ii) To identify the minimal polynomial, use a known extension degree or prove irreducibility by the degree-2/32/32/3 root test, Eisenstein, or irreducible reduction modulo a prime.

(iii) Only after identifying the minimal polynomial, read its degree, trace and norm from its coefficients.

Worked example

If α\alphaα is a root of x3+x−3x^3+x-3x3+x−3, then modulo 222 the polynomial becomes x3+x+1x^3+x+1x3+x+1, which takes the value 111 at both elements of F2\F_2F2​. It is therefore irreducible, so minpolyα,Q=x3+x−3\mipy_{\alpha,\Q}=x^3+x-3minpolyα,Q​=x3+x−3, tr(α)=0\tr\bra\alpha=0tr(α)=0 and N(α)=3N\bra\alpha=3N(α)=3.

methods.title: Run a Diophantine ideal-power argument
methods.bodyHtml:
Recognise. Solve or constrain a Mordell-type equation by factoring it in a quadratic ring of integers.

Write first. Apply local congruence checks, then factor the equation into conjugate principal ideals.

Solution route.

(i) Assume a prime ideal divides both conjugate factors; add or subtract their generators to restrict the rational prime below it.

(ii) Exclude those finitely many primes and conclude that the factors are coprime.

(iii) Use unique ideal factorisation to extract ideal powers.

(iv) Use the class-group order to principalise the ideal.

(v) Restore the unit multiplier and compare coefficients.

Worked example

If a prime ideal divides both (y+−41)\bra{y+\sqrt{-41}}(y+−41​) and (y−−41)\bra{y-\sqrt{-41}}(y−−41​), then it contains 2−412\sqrt{-41}2−41​; primality forces it to lie above 222 or 414141. After those cases are excluded, the conjugate ideals are coprime and the cube-ideal step becomes valid.

Stop when. Every possible common prime divisor and every unit multiplier has been handled, and coefficient comparison gives all solutions or the required contradiction.

Fatal checks. Never infer coprimality from the elements alone; never replace equality of principal ideals by equality of generators without a unit.
